findings: File: js/apps/account-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v3/account/messages/messages_en.properties, Line: 188, Issue: Unsupported format syntax: The message now uses ICU/ChoiceFormat syntax (`{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`). The account UI renders message properties with its own lightweight JS formatter, which historically supports only simple positional placeholders like `{0}` and does not implement `choice` subformats. If that is the case here, users will see the raw pattern text (e.g. "at most {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}") instead of a formatted count. Worth verifying that the JS-side message renderer in this PR actually handles `choice` before merging; if it does not, the message should be reworded to avoid the syntax.

File: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java, Line: 88, Issue: Missing English key handling: `getEnglishValue` returns an empty string when a key is missing from the English bundle. For a translation key that doesn't exist in the English file, `containsHtml("")` is false, so `POLICY_NO_HTML` is applied and any legitimate HTML in the translation (e.g. a `
` or `` tag) is reported as "Illegal HTML", with a confusing message comparing against an empty English source. It would be clearer to skip the check (or report a distinct "key missing in English file" error) in this case.

File: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java, Line: 60, Issue: Wrong exception type: `verifySafeHtml` throws raw `RuntimeException` on IO errors, while the surrounding `verify()` method correctly wraps IO failures in `MojoExecutionException`. A failure reading the file or the derived English file will bypass the Maven plugin's error handling and surface as an unhandled runtime exception instead of a proper build error with the plugin's context.

File: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java, Line: 113, Issue: Anchor removal mismatch: In `santizeAnchors`, when a translation anchor matches an English anchor, `value.replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), "")` removes the *first* occurrence of that tag string in the translation, not necessarily the occurrence the matcher just found. If the same anchor tag appears multiple times with different surrounding text, the accounting between translation and English anchors can drift, potentially allowing an extra unmatched anchor to slip through or falsely flagging a valid one. Matching counts explicitly (or removing by matcher region) would be more robust.

File: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java, Line: 60, Issue: Duplicate file read: `verify()` already reads the file contents via `Files.readString`, then `verifySafeHtml` re-opens and parses the same file a second time through `FileInputStream`. The already-read `contents` string could be parsed once and shared, avoiding redundant I/O and the possibility of the two reads seeing different file states.

findings: File: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py, Line: 143, Issue: Data loss on processing failure: In `OrderedQueueWorker.run`, if `result_processor` raises, the exception is logged but the `finally` block still calls `complete_offset`. Since the offset was added via `add_offset` in `submit`, the offset now appears processed, and the commit loop will advance `last_committed` past it even though the message was never successfully handled. Any consumer relying on the commit guarantee ("Only commits offsets after successful processing" per the class docstring) will silently lose that message on restart. If at-most-once semantics are intentional, the docstring and metric naming should say so; otherwise failed items need a retry/dead-letter path before the offset is completed.

File: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py, Line: 337, Issue: Commit after terminate: `terminate()` sets `shutdown_event` but never joins `commit_thread`, unlike `close()`. The commit thread waits on `shutdown_event.wait(1.0)` and can wake up one more time after termination, calling `commit_function` concurrently with (or after) the strategy has been torn down. Depending on what `commit_function` does (e.g., producer commit on a closed producer), this can raise or commit offsets at an unsafe point during shutdown.

File: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py, Line: 296, Issue: Assert for control flow: `submit` uses `assert isinstance(message.value, BrokerValue)` to extract the partition/offset. Under `python -O` asserts are stripped, and `message.value.partition` would then raise `AttributeError` on a non-BrokerValue, which is caught by the broad `except Exception` and silently swallowed (offset never tracked). A explicit check with proper handling would be safer.

File: tests/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/test_queue_consumer.py, Line: 116, Issue: Flaky test: `test_different_groups_distributed` asserts that 20 group keys hash to exactly 3 distinct queue indices. With hash-based assignment there is no guarantee that all 3 queues are hit — a hash function that maps the 20 generated keys to only 2 buckets (or a future change of hashing scheme) makes this assertion fail intermittently or after refactoring. The test should assert the count is <= num_queues (or that assignment is valid), not exactly equal to the queue count.

File: tests/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/test_queue_consumer.py, Line: 195, Issue: Timing-dependent assertion: In `test_stats_reporting`, `stats["total_items"] > 0` is checked immediately after submitting 10 items, but background workers may have already drained the queues by then, making the assertion flaky. Similarly, the later assertion `stats["total_items"] == 0` right after the completion event can race if items are still being accounted for. These stats checks should be retried/polled with a timeout rather than asserted once.

File: tests/sentry/uptime/consumers/test_results_consumer.py, Line: 2130, Issue: Flaky Kafka assertion: In the Kafka integration test, `verify_consumer.committed(partitions)` is called immediately after `processor._shutdown()` with no timeout or retry. Depending on timing (the ONCE_PER_SECOND commit policy plus async broker group coordination), `committed()` can return `OFFSET_INVALID` (-1001) or a stale offset even when a commit was made, making `committed[0].offset == 5` flaky. Consider polling `committed()` with a timeout until it reflects the expected offset, or asserting against `commits_made` (which is already tracked) as the source of truth.

File: tests/sentry/uptime/consumers/test_results_consumer.py, Line: 2098, Issue: Private API usage: The integration test drives the arroyo `StreamProcessor` via private methods `processor._run_once()` and `processor._shutdown()`. These are not part of arroyo's public contract and can break silently on arroyo upgrades. If a public run/stop API (or a test helper) exists, prefer it; otherwise this coupling should be noted.

File: tests/sentry/uptime/consumers/test_results_consumer.py, Line: 1900, Issue: Fixed side_effect list: In `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling`, `mock_processor_call.side_effect = [Exception("Processing failed"), None]` is a fixed-length list. If the implementation ever retries a failed message (now or after a future change), the third call raises `StopIteration` inside a worker thread, which can mask the actual behavior under test and make the failure hard to diagnose. A callable side effect that fails only on the first call per message would be more robust.

findings: File: packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx, Line: 100, Issue: Hardcoded locale: The cache timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` instead of the user's locale. The component already uses `useLocale()` for translations, so the timestamp will render in US format for all users regardless of their locale preference. Use the locale from `useLocale()` (or `Intl.DateTimeFormat()` with no locale argument) instead.

File: packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx, Line: 40, Issue: Stale cache status: `deleteCacheMutation` shows a success toast and calls `onSuccess?.()`, but unlike `disconnectMutation` it never invalidates the relevant tRPC queries (e.g. `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`). After deleting the cache, any parent view that reads cache status will keep showing the old "cache last updated" entry until a full refetch happens elsewhere.

File: packages/lib/server/repository/selectedCalendar.ts, Line: 400, Issue: Possible Type Bug: `updateManyByCredentialId` declares its `data` parameter as `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput`, but Prisma's `updateMany` expects `SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput` (the updateMany mutation input type). `SelectedCalendarUpdateInput` allows nested relation-style fields (e.g., object-shaped relation updates) that `updateMany` does not support, so callers could pass a `data` object that type-checks at this signature but fails at runtime or at the actual `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany` call site. Using `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput` would align the signature with the underlying query.

File: packages/prisma/schema.prisma, Line: 1718, Issue: Misleading comment: The comment claims `@updatedAt` provides an initial value for "future raw inserts", but Prisma's `@updatedAt` is applied only by Prisma Client on create/update operations; raw SQL inserts (or writes from other tools bypassing Prisma Client) will not populate or update `updatedAt` unless the database itself has a default. If raw inserts are a real use case, a database-level default (e.g., `@default(now())` mapped to a DB default via `prisma migrate` with `DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`) is needed. Also note legacy rows will get the migration timestamp as their `updatedAt`, not their actual last-update time, which may be acceptable but is worth confirming.

File: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/_router.tsx, Line: 28, Issue: Possible authorization gap: The new `deleteCache` mutation accepts an arbitrary `credentialId` from the client. The handler implementation is not visible in this diff, so it may well validate ownership, but if `deleteCacheHandler` does not verify that the credential belongs to `ctx.user`, any authenticated user could delete another user's calendar cache by guessing/enumerating credential IDs. Worth confirming the ownership check exists in `deleteCache.handler`.

File: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.ts, Line: 33, Issue: Possible Bug: `cacheStatusMap.get(calendar.credentialId) || null` uses falsy coercion instead of a nullish check. If `updatedAt` is a valid timestamp, this is fine, but if `updatedAt` could ever be an epoch value of 0 or the repository returns a falsy-but-valid value, it would be silently converted to `null`. More concretely: `Map.get` returning `undefined` (credential not found in cache) and an actual cached entry with a falsy `updatedAt` are conflated. Use `?? null` to distinguish "no cache entry" from "falsy timestamp".

File: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.ts, Line: 27, Issue: Extra DB query: A new `CalendarCacheRepository` query is added on every `connectedCalendars` call, which is a frequently invoked viewer endpoint. If `connectedCalendars` is empty, `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` is still called with an empty array — worth verifying the repository handles an empty `credentialIds` list without issuing a pointless query or a Prisma `findMany` with an `in: []` filter (which returns empty but still hits the DB).

File: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh, Line: 68, Issue: Portability Bug: `sed -i '' -E ...` is macOS/BSD syntax only. On Linux (GNU sed), `-i` takes an optional suffix argument, so `''` is treated as the input file name and the script fails with "sed: can't read : No such file or directory", leaving `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` unupdated. Use a portable form, e.g. detect sed flavor or use `sed -i.bak`.

File: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh, Line: 10, Issue: Wrong exit code: `cleanup` always calls `exit 0`, including on the failure paths (rate limit hit, failed URL extraction). Callers and CI will see the script as successful even though no tunnel URL was obtained and the env file was never updated. It should exit non-zero on failure.

File: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh, Line: 30, Issue: Reuse path fragile: When an existing tmole process is detected, the URL is read from `$LOG_FILE`, but the log is only created/reset when this script starts tmole itself. If tmole was started elsewhere (or the log was rotated/deleted), `extract_url_from_log` returns empty and the script exits via cleanup without a clear diagnostic distinguishing "reuse failed" from "startup failed".

findings: File: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go, Line: 237, Issue: Possible Bug: `createTestAnnotations` now explicitly assigns `ID: int64(i + 1)` to every annotation before bulk-inserting them. If the old-annotation loop (not shown in this hunk) does not also set explicit IDs, those inserts will rely on the table's auto-increment, which typically starts at 1 and will collide with the explicitly inserted IDs 1..N, causing duplicate-key failures on databases that enforce primary key uniqueness (e.g., MySQL/Postgres). Even if all inserts set explicit IDs, on Postgres the sequence is not advanced by explicit-ID inserts, so any later auto-increment insert in the same test DB can fail. Verify both loops assign IDs consistently or drop the explicit IDs.

File: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go, Line: 98, Issue: Test performance: The new test case creates 40003 annotations plus 80006 tag rows to exercise a batch size of 32767. Even with the 500-row `InsertMulti` batching, this makes an already-integration-scoped test substantially slower and more resource-heavy; consider whether a smaller count just above the SQLite variable limit (e.g., ~33000) would suffice, or at least confirm CI tolerates the added runtime.

File: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go, Line: 531, Issue: Incorrect log level: The new cleanup paths use `r.log.Error` for routine, successful progress messages ("Annotations to clean by time", "cleaned annotations by time", "Tags to clean", etc.). These fire on every cleanup batch and will flood error logs/alerting on healthy systems, and each message also logs `err` even when it is nil. These should be Debug/Info level, and the full `ids` list should not be logged (it can be thousands of entries per batch).

File: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go, Line: 630, Issue: Possible infinite loop: `untilDoneOrCancelled` terminates only when a batch reports zero affected rows, but the loop condition is based on `affected`, not on whether IDs were found. If `fetchIDs` returns a non-empty ID list but `deleteByIDs` reports 0 affected rows (e.g., the rows were deleted concurrently between the SELECT and the DELETE, or the driver misreports RowsAffected), the same IDs are re-fetched and re-deleted forever with no progress. Consider terminating when the fetched ID list is empty, or bounding retries when affected == 0 despite non-empty IDs.

File: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go, Line: 596, Issue: SQL built via string concat: `fetchIDs` interpolates `table` and `condition` directly into the SQL string. This is not currently exploitable since both come from internal constants, but the new `deleteByIDs` carefully parameterizes IDs while `fetchIDs` does not, which is inconsistent and fragile if a caller ever passes user-influenced input. Low severity given current call sites.

File: pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go, Line: 77, Issue: Possible debug leftover: The cleanup ticker interval was reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute. If this change was made to speed up manual testing, it looks like a debug value accidentally left in: running the cleanup job every minute increases database load (especially given the PR title mentions deadlock-prone cleanup queries on MySQL) for no stated benefit. If the more frequent interval is intentional, it should be documented or made configurable.

In a test fake, callers that extract a logger from a context (e.g., code under test calling `logger.FromContext(ctx)` and then logging) will record calls on a fresh `TestLogger`, so assertions made against the original `TestLogger` (its `Logs`/`Calls` fields) will fail or silently pass with zero calls. Returning `f` (or a logger sharing the same recording state) would preserve the fake's contract.

File: pkg/plugins/log/ifaces.go, Line: 20, Issue: Breaking interface change: Adding `FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger` to the `Logger` interface is a breaking change for any external or internal type that implements `Logger` but does not have this method; all such implementations will fail to compile until updated. If this is intentional (e.g., all implementers are updated elsewhere in this PR), it can be ignored, but external plugin authors implementing `Logger` will also be affected.

File: pkg/plugins/log/logger.go, Line: 48, Issue: Silent fallback loses context logger: `FromContext` type-asserts the result of `d.l.FromContext(ctx)` to `*log.ConcreteLogger`, and on failure silently returns `d.New()` — the wrapper's default logger — instead of the logger stored in the context. If the assertion fails (e.g., the infra package stores a different concrete type or a value rather than a pointer in the context), callers will log to the wrong logger with no error or indication. Consider logging a warning on the fallback path, or verifying that the assertion matches how the infra package actually stores loggers in contexts.

If this exclusion is intentional (e.g., long-lived streams), a comment explaining it would help reviewers and future maintainers.

Given the PR renames instrumentation middleware to metrics middleware, keeping an "instrument*" name here may cause confusion between the two middlewares. Consider a name like withContextualLogger.

File: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go, Line: 52, Issue: Loss of log context: The refactor removes `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `uname`, `traceID`, `dsName`, and `dsUID` from the "Plugin Request Completed" log line. findings: File: pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go, Line: 30, Issue: Cache key collision: The new `userPermDenialCacheKey` builds the key by naive string concatenation with `_` separators, without escaping or a fixed-length encoding. Since user UIDs, actions, names, and parents can themselves contain underscores, distinct tuples can produce identical keys (e.g., `name="a_b", parent="c"` and `name="a", parent="b_c"` both yield `ns.perm_<user>_<action>_a_b_c`). A cached denial for one resource would then be wrongly returned for another, denying a user access they should have. Using a delimiter that cannot appear in the components (or hashing/encoding the components) avoids this.

File: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go, Line: 116, Issue: Stale denial cache: The new denial cache is checked before the permission cache and is never invalidated or overwritten when access is later granted. Scenario: a user's check is denied at T0, so the denial is cached. An admin then grants the user the permission and the permission cache is refreshed (e.g., via another request that populates `permCache` with allowed=true). Subsequent `Check` calls still short-circuit on the denial cache entry and return `Allowed: false` for the remainder of `shortCacheTTL`, even though fresh permissions allow the action. Since the full-check path (which would set allowed=true) never deletes the denial key, the denial persists independently of the permission cache's own TTL/invalidation. Consider deleting the denial key whenever a check succeeds, or invalidating it on permission changes.

File: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go, Line: 153, Issue: Denial cached on stale data: When `getCachedIdentityPermissions` returns a cached permission set and `checkPermission` yields allowed=false, the code falls through to the full DB path and re-checks — good. However, if that full path also denies, the denial is written to `permDenialCache` keyed only by namespace/user/action/name/parentFolder. The denial may have been produced from a cached permission snapshot that is itself stale (e.g., permissions were just revoked and later restored within `shortCacheTTL`), extending the effective staleness window beyond the permission cache TTL. This is a lower-severity consistency concern tied to the same invalidation gap as the stale-denial issue.

File: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go, Line: 339, Issue: Coverage loss: The removed test case "should return permissions from cache if available" in TestService_getUserPermissions is the only test that covered the cache-hit path of getUserPermissions. Since this PR changes how permission caching behaves (adding a denial cache and cache-aware Check/List), removing this case without a replacement reduces coverage of exactly the code path being modified. Consider re-adding an equivalent cache-hit test for getUserPermissions.

File: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go, Line: 893, Issue: Missing deny-on-miss test: The new TestService_CacheCheck covers allow-on-cache-hit, fallback-on-miss, fallback-on-outdated-cache, and explicit denial, but has no case asserting that Check denies when the cache contains an explicit false entry for the requested resource (e.g., permCache with {"dashboards:uid:dash1": false} and no denial cache entry). Without it, a regression that treats cached false as "not cached" and falls back to the store would go undetected.

File: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go, Line: 100, Issue: Race condition: The limit check in `CreateOrUpdateDevice` is a non-atomic count-then-insert: two concurrent requests for different new devices can both observe `count < deviceLimit` and both insert, exceeding the limit. Under concurrent traffic the configured limit can be silently surpassed. Consider enforcing the limit atomically (e.g., insert guarded by a conditional statement or transaction with a lock).

File: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go, Line: 72, Issue: Error semantics: `updateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` whenever `rowsAffected == 0`, but this also occurs when the device exists yet its `updated_at` falls outside the 30-day window (e.g., a caller passes a device with an old `UpdatedAt`, or clock skew between the count's `time.Now()` anchor and the device's `UpdatedAt`). In that case the error misreports the cause, and a genuinely stale existing device is never refreshed. The window anchor should be consistent (e.g., use `time.Now()` in both places) or the error should distinguish "not found/stale" from "limit reached".

File: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go, Line: 44, Issue: Synchronous tagging on request path: TagDevice was previously run in a background goroutine with its own 2-minute timeout and panic recovery, so failures or slowness never affected authentication. It is now called synchronously with the request's context on every anonymous authentication. If the backing store (anonstore) is slow or unavailable, every anonymous request will block or fail until the store responds, turning a previously non-blocking side effect into a latency/availability risk on the hot authentication path. Consider keeping the call asynchronous or bounding it with a timeout.

File: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go, Line: 44, Issue: Request context for tagging: The new call passes the request-scoped ctx instead of a detached context. If the client disconnects or the request is cancelled mid-authentication, TagDevice will be cancelled and the device may never be tagged/recorded, defeating the device-limit accounting. The old code deliberately used context.Background() with a timeout to avoid this.

File: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go, Line: 144, Issue: Behavior change: `TagDevice` now returns the error from `tagDeviceUI` instead of only logging it and returning nil. This changes the contract for all callers: previously a UI-tagging failure was non-fatal (logged at Debug level and swallowed), now it propagates. If any caller treats a returned error as fatal (e.g., aborting a request or login flow), a transient UI-tag failure will now fail that flow. Verify this propagation is intentional and that callers handle it, or keep logging-and-continuing if UI tagging is best-effort.

findings: File: packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts, Line: 273, Issue: Brittle assertions: The new assertions compare `Prisma.sql` objects with `toEqual` against hand-written SQL strings (e.g. `Prisma.sql`("userId" = ${...}) AND ("teamId" IS NULL)``). `Prisma.Sql` equality depends on the exact internal `strings`/`values` arrays, including whitespace and parenthesization of the implementation's generated SQL. Any harmless reformatting of the raw SQL in the service (spacing, paren grouping, `TRUE` vs `true`) will break these tests even when behavior is identical. Consider asserting on the semantic result (rows returned via a raw query, as done in the `getBaseConditions` test) or normalizing the SQL string before comparison.

File: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts, Line: 170, Issue: Possible Bug: `Prisma.sql` does not correctly interpolate a raw JavaScript array as a single parameter. In `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}))`, `("userId" = ANY(${uniqueUserIds}))`, and `("userId" = ANY(${userIdsFromTeam}))`, the array interpolation will not produce the intended single array/bind parameter the way `teamId: { in: [...] }` did in the old Prisma filter. The safe pattern is `Prisma.join(teamIds)` (e.g., `"teamId" IN (${Prisma.join(teamIds)})`) or passing a properly typed array. As written, these authorization conditions may throw at query time or produce incorrect SQL, which would break org/team scoping for the insights queries.

File: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts, Line: 68, Issue: Removed public API: The `findMany` method was removed and replaced by `getBaseConditions`, which now returns raw `Prisma.Sql` instead of executing a query and returning booking records. Any caller that previously used `service.findMany(...)` to fetch rows will break unless it was migrated in the rest of the PR; the new contract also pushes responsibility for table name, select columns, and `$queryRaw` usage onto callers, which is easy to get wrong (e.g., forgetting to pass the returned SQL as a WHERE fragment on `bookingTimeStatusDenormalized`).

findings: File: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts, Line: 253, Issue: Possible Bug: In `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent`, the fallback lookup `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. In that case, comparing `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` compares against `undefined`, so the `find` will (at best) match an entry with no externalId or return `undefined`, making `calendarId`/`selectedCalendar` `undefined` instead of the destination calendar's externalId as before. Previously the code used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` directly. A realistic trigger: updating/deleting an event without passing an explicit `externalCalendarId` now targets the wrong calendar (or fails), whereas before it used the destination calendar. The lookup likely should match on `credentialId` (as done in `createEvent`) or fall back to the first destination calendar.

File: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts, Line: 145, Issue: Silent fallback: In `createEvent`, if no destination calendar matches the given `credentialId`, `selectedCalendar` is `undefined` and the code silently falls back to `"primary"`. Combined with the new multi-host flow, a mismatched `credentialId` (e.g., a stale or wrong credential passed by the caller) would cause the event to be created on the organizer's primary calendar instead of the intended shared calendar, with no error or log to surface the mismatch. Consider logging or rejecting when no matching destination calendar is found.

File: packages/core/CalendarManager.ts, Line: 220, Issue: Unused parameter: The new `externalId` parameter is accepted but never used inside `createEvent` - it is only echoed back in the returned result. If the intent (per the PR title, handling multiple hosts on destinationCalendar) was to derive or validate the external ID from the credential/selected calendar, that logic is missing; callers passing a wrong or empty `externalId` will get it propagated verbatim into the event result. If it is intentionally just a pass-through, consider documenting that, since the signature suggests the function is responsible for resolving it.

File: packages/core/CalendarManager.ts, Line: 230, Issue: Unverified interface change: `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` now passes a second argument to the calendar adapter. If any calendar implementation's `createEvent` signature does not accept this extra argument (TypeScript would catch it only if all adapters share a strict typed interface), the value is silently ignored or, for adapters using positional params differently, could be misinterpreted. Worth confirming all calendar app implementations were updated in this PR.

File: packages/core/EventManager.ts, Line: 117, Issue: Possible Bug: The new destructuring `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when `destinationCalendar` is not set, and the following condition then accesses `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, so bookings without a destinationCalendar worked; now any such booking with `location === MeetLocationType` will throw a TypeError ("Cannot read properties of undefined") instead of falling back to Cal Video. Should be `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

File: packages/core/EventManager.ts, Line: 508, Issue: Possible Bug: In `updateAllCalendarEvents`, when a reference has a `credentialId` that is neither in `this.calendarCredentials` nor resolvable from the DB (e.g., the DB lookup returns null, or the credential has no `app.slug`), `credential` remains `undefined` and `updateEvent(undefined, event, ...)` is still pushed into `result`. This will likely throw inside `updateEvent` (or fail the update) for that reference, whereas the pre-existing DB-fetch fallback in `createAllCalendarEvents` at least guards with `if (credential)`. The loop should skip pushing when no credential could be resolved.

File: packages/core/builders/CalendarEvent/class.ts, Line: 26, Issue: Type change ripple: The `destinationCalendar` property type changes from a single `DestinationCalendar` to `DestinationCalendar[]`. This is a breaking contract change for any existing consumer of `CalendarEventClass` that reads or writes `destinationCalendar` as a single object (e.g., `event.destinationCalendar.userId` or passing a single object). Within the shown diff there is no code updating such usages or normalizing the value, so any code path still assigning a single object will now silently violate the declared type (and array operations like `.map` on it would fail at runtime). Verify all producers/consumers of this field were updated in the rest of the PR.

File: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts, Line: 440, Issue: Duplicate deletions: The outer loop now iterates over every calendar reference, but the recurring-event branch inside the loop still iterates over ALL of the user's calendar credentials and deletes events for every updated booking. With multiple calendar references (the multi-host scenario this PR targets), the same set of events will be deleted once per reference, producing N duplicate deleteEvent API calls (and N entries in `apiDeletes`). The recurring branch should either run once outside the reference loop or be scoped to the current reference's credential/uid.

File: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts, Line: 445, Issue: Only first reference deleted per booking: Inside the recurring branch, `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))` picks only the first calendar reference of each updated booking. For multi-host bookings each updated booking can have several calendar references, so events on the other hosts' calendars will never be deleted — contradicting the PR's goal of handling multiple destination calendars. `find` should be `filter` (or otherwise iterate all matching refs), consistent with the change made to `bookingCalendarReference`.

File: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts, Line: 424, Issue: Unhandled credential fallback: When the credential is not found in `bookingToDelete.user.credentials`, it is fetched from the DB via `prisma.credential.findUnique`. If that lookup also returns null (e.g., the credential was deleted after the booking was created), `calendarCredential` stays undefined and the event is silently never deleted from the calendar, with no logging or fallback. A stale reference for a removed credential therefore leaves orphaned calendar events.

File: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts, Line: 1874, Issue: Dropped calendars: Multiple destination calendars are collected into `evt.destinationCalendar` (event-type + organizer + team members), but the booking creation only connects `evt.destinationCalendar[0]`. The remaining collected calendars are discarded, so for a COLLECTIVE event the intended per-member calendar handling (per the original comment) does not actually persist beyond the first entry. If only the first is intentionally connected, the push of `teamDestinationCalendars` into `evt` is misleading dead data.

File: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts, Line: 729, Issue: Removed select field: The dynamic-booking `prisma.user.findMany` select no longer includes `organization: { select: { slug: true } }`. File: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts, Line: 724, Issue: Wrong error status: The validation errors thrown inside `loadUsers` (e.g., "dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty.") are plain `Error`s, so the catch block maps them to a 500 "Unable to load users" instead of a client-appropriate 4xx. File: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/editLocation.handler.ts, Line: 85, Issue: Possible double-wrapping: The new code unconditionally wraps `booking.destinationCalendar` in an array (`[booking?.destinationCalendar]`). If the field is guaranteed to be a single object, this is fine — but that assumption should be verified or guarded (e.g., `Array.isArray` check).

File: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts, Line: 151, Issue: Possible Bug: The refactor inverts the condition for `slug`. Previously, `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` included `slug` in the organization `create` payload only when team billing was NOT enabled. The new ternary `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` includes `slug` only when billing IS enabled. findings: File: apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx, Line: 7, Issue: Naming Mismatch: The component is defined as `TwoFactor` in a file named `BackupCode.tsx`, and it renders a backup-code input, not a generic 2FA input. The misleading name can confuse consumers importing this component (e.g., someone looking for a TOTP code input may import `TwoFactor` expecting a different UI). Rename the component to match its purpose.

File: apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx, Line: 22, Issue: Weak Input Validation: Validation relies only on `minLength={10}` / `maxLength={11}`. Any 10-11 character string (e.g., "aaaaaaaaaaaa" or "12345") passes, and a user can also enter a dash in the wrong position (e.g., "XXXXXX-XXXX" is 11 chars). Since backup codes are consumed server-side, a malformed value will only fail after submission. Consider a `pattern` (e.g., `^[A-Z0-9]{5}-[A-Z0-9]{5}$` or the dash-less equivalent) to fail fast client-side.

File: apps/web/components/settings/DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx, Line: 103, Issue: Form field registration: `handleDisable` destructures `backupCode` from form values and passes it to `TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable`, but unlike the password field (which is rendered via `PasswordField` with `...form.register("password")` elsewhere), the `BackupCode` component is rendered without any visible registration into the react-hook-form instance. If `BackupCode` does not internally call `form.register("backupCode")` (it receives no form props here), `backupCode` will always be `undefined` and the "lost access" flow will silently submit without a backup code. Verify the component registers the field or pass the registration down explicitly.

File: apps/web/components/settings/DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx, Line: 118, Issue: Stale error message on toggle: When the user toggles between TOTP and backup-code modes via the "lost access"/"go back" button, `resetForm(false)` clears `backupCode`/`totpCode` but the previous submission error (e.g. "incorrect 2fa code") remains displayed under the newly switched input, which can confuse users into thinking the new mode also failed. Consider clearing `errorMessage` on toggle or moving the error display next to the active input.

File: apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx, Line: 68, Issue: State not reset: `resetState()` clears the password, error message, and step, but does not clear `backupCodes` or `backupCodesUrl`. After the modal is closed and reopened, the previously generated backup codes (and their blob URL) remain in state. If the user re-runs setup, stale codes from a prior generation could briefly be displayed, and the old blob URL is only revoked when a new one is created — never on dialog close/unmount, leaking the object URL (which contains the backup codes) for the lifetime of the page.

File: apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx, Line: 261, Issue: Dismissal path skips onEnable: When the flow reaches `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes`, the cancel button is hidden and the only way to finish is the custom "close" button, which calls `resetState()` and `onEnable()`. However, the Dialog can still be dismissed via the backdrop/escape key (`onOpenChange`), which calls neither. In that case `onEnable()` is never invoked even though 2FA was successfully enabled (the enable endpoint already returned 200 before this step), leaving the parent component unaware that 2FA is now active. The backup codes are also lost without download/copy in that path.

File: apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx, Line: 62, Issue: Possible Bug: `const [backupCodes, setBackupCodes] = useState([])` infers the state type as `never[]` in TypeScript, so `setBackupCodes(body.backupCodes)` (where `body` is untyped JSON from `response.json()`) either fails to typecheck or silently widens. Additionally, `body.backupCodes` is used without any validation — if the response shape differs (e.g., codes returned as an object or missing), `body.backupCodes.map(...)` will throw at runtime inside `handleSetup`. Consider typing the state as `string[]` and guarding the response shape.

File: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts, Line: 55, Issue: Possible Bug: `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` is called without error handling. If `user.backupCodes` contains malformed or legacy data (or decryption produces garbage due to a key mismatch), `JSON.parse` will throw and the request will fail with an unhandled 500 instead of a clean error response. Wrap it in try/catch and return `ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes` or a similar client-facing error.

File: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts, Line: 60, Issue: Backup code consumption unclear: The comment states "we delete all stored backup codes at the end", but in the visible disable flow the only mutation is `backupCodes: null` in the final `prisma` update, which runs regardless of whether a backup code or TOTP was used. findings: File: packages/app-store/_utils/getCalendar.ts, Line: 15, Issue: Unhandled import rejection: The function now awaits `appStore[calendarType.split("_").join("")]`, implying the store entries are async (dynamic) imports. If such an import fails (e.g., a broken/missing calendar package, or a chunk-load failure at runtime), the promise rejection propagates uncaught to every caller of `getCalendar`, whereas previously the synchronous lookup could not throw for a missing entry. There is no try/catch or `.catch` here, so a single bad calendar type can crash the flow that resolves credentials. Consider wrapping the await and returning `null` (with a log) on failure, matching the existing "not implemented" fallback path. Note: this depends on how `appStore` entries are defined elsewhere in the PR, which is not shown in this diff.

File: packages/app-store/_utils/getCalendar.ts, Line: 15, Issue: Possible shape mismatch: After awaiting, `calendarApp` is presumably a module namespace object rather than the previous app-store entry object. The subsequent check `"lib" in calendarApp && "CalendarService" in calendarApp.lib` only holds if `lib` is a named export of each dynamically imported module. If any package exports its calendar service under a different shape (e.g., default export containing `lib`), the check will fail and the calendar will be silently reported as "not implemented". Worth verifying all entries in `appStore` export `lib` at the top level. This is contingent on the (unseen) new definitions of the store entries.

File: packages/app-store/index.ts, Line: 3, Issue: Type contract change: Each entry in `appStore` changes from a module namespace object to a `Promise<module>` (dynamic `import()` returns a Promise). Any consumer that previously accessed exports synchronously, e.g. `appStore.googlecalendar.someExport`, will now receive `undefined` unless it awaits the promise first. All call sites of `appStore` must be updated to `await` (or `.then()`) the resolved module; if any consumer was not updated in this PR, it will break at runtime. Also note the resolved module is under `.default` when the underlying files use `export default`, which consumers must handle.

File: packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts, Line: 125, Issue: Unhandled async in forEach: The callback passed to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach` is now `async`, but `forEach` does not await the returned promises. Two consequences: (1) the surrounding `try/catch` will not catch any rejection from `calendar?.deleteEvent`, `deleteMeeting`, or `getCalendar`, so a failed calendar/video deletion becomes an unhandled promise rejection and reschedule continues as if deletion succeeded; (2) the deletions no longer run to completion before the function returns. Using `for...of` with `await` (or `Promise.all` over a mapped array) inside the `try` block would restore the intended error handling and sequencing.

File: packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts, Line: 125, Issue: Unawaited async callback: Passing an `async` callback to `Array.forEach` means the returned promises are not awaited. The surrounding `try` block can no longer catch errors from `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` or `deleteMeeting(...)`, so a failed calendar/video deletion will be silently swallowed (unhandled promise rejection) and `Reschedule` will report success even when deletions failed. If sequential or awaited deletion is intended, use a `for...of` loop with `await`, or `Promise.all` with `map` if parallel deletion is acceptable.

File: packages/core/CalendarManager.ts, Line: 28, Issue: Possible Bug: `getCalendar` is now asynchronous (as evidenced by the `await getCalendar(credential)` changes in `createEvent`, `updateEvent`, and `deleteEvent`), but in `getCalendarCredentials` the call `const calendar = getCalendar(credential)` is not awaited. Each entry pushed into `credentials` will contain a `calendar` that is a Promise rather than a calendar instance. Any consumer of the returned credentials that reads `calendar` (e.g., to check availability or list events) will operate on a Promise object and fail or behave incorrectly. This call should be awaited (e.g., make the map callback async and `await getCalendar(credential)`).

File: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts, Line: 458, Issue: async callback in forEach: The `.forEach(async (credential) => { ... })` callback now contains `await getCalendar(credential)` and an inner loop awaiting calendar operations. `forEach` does not wait for async callbacks, so these deletions run detached: the enclosing handler can complete (and the request finish) before the calendar events are deleted, and any rejection from `getCalendar` or the delete calls becomes an unhandled promise rejection with no logging or propagation. Converting this to a `for...of` loop (as done for the legacy path further below) or collecting promises and awaiting them would fix it.

File: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts, Line: 474, Issue: Sequential awaits in loop: The legacy-path loop now awaits `getCalendar(credential)` sequentially for each credential. For credentials with many calendars or frequently polled availability, this adds a potentially large write workload per call even when nothing meaningful changed. File: src/sentry/monitors/logic/incident_occurrence.py, Line: 138, Issue: Possible Bug: `get_failure_reason` filters `failed_checkins` to statuses present in `HUMAN_FAILURE_STATUS_MAP`. If the list contains only statuses outside that map (or is empty), `status_counts` is empty: the singular branch is skipped (sum is 0, not 1), and the plural branch produces `" check-ins detected"` via `get_text_list([])`. If callers can pass such input (e.g., a check-in with an unexpected status), the evidence string is malformed; consider guarding against an empty `status_counts`.

File: src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py, Line: 36, Issue: Non-deterministic check-in ordering: The query filtering previous check-ins orders only by `-date_added` with no tiebreaker (e.g. `id`). When multiple check-ins share the same `date_added` timestamp (common for cron monitors that check in on a fixed schedule, or bursts of check-ins written in the same transaction/second), the slice of `failure_issue_threshold` rows may nondeterministically include or exclude the failed check-in or an older OK check-in. This can cause the incident's `starting_checkin` to vary between runs, or an OK check-in within the threshold window to be missed/incorrectly included when deciding whether an incident state was reached. Adding a secondary ordering key (e.g. `-id`) would make the window deterministic.

File: src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py, Line: 92, Issue: Possible duplicate occurrences: In the OK/ACTIVE branch, the code loops over every check-in in the threshold window (`checkins = MonitorCheckIn.objects.filter(id__in=[...])`) and calls `create_incident_occurrence` once per check-in, all with the same `previous_checkins` list and the same incident. If that function is idempotent per check-in this is fine, but this should be verified since the loop passes the full `previous_checkins` list on every iteration rather than the individual `checkin`'s context.

findings: File: pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go, Line: 30, Issue: Cache key collision: The new `userPermDenialCacheKey` builds keys by naive string concatenation with `_` separators, the same scheme used by `userPermCacheKey`. The two formats can produce identical strings: `userPermCacheKey(ns, "u", "a_name_parent")` yields `ns.perm_u_a_name_parent`, which equals `userPermDenialCacheKey(ns, "u", "a", "name", "parent")`. Since actions (and user UIDs/names) commonly contain underscores, a denial-cache entry could collide with a regular permission-cache entry, returning a cached denial for a legitimate permission check (or vice versa). Using a delimiter that cannot appear in the components (or a structured/encoded key) would avoid this.

File: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go, Line: 116, Issue: Stale denial cache: The new `permDenialCache` is consulted before the permission cache and is never invalidated when a user's permissions change. Scenario: a check is denied and cached in `permDenialCache`; afterwards an admin grants the user the permission. Even once `permCache` is refreshed with the allowed result, `Check` short-circuits on the denial-cache hit at the top of the function and returns `Allowed: false` for up to `shortCacheTTL`. If permission changes elsewhere in the codebase delete `permCache` entries to make grants take effect immediately, that invalidation does not cover `permDenialCache`, so grants will be delayed by the TTL. If no such invalidation exists, the delay is bounded by `shortCacheTTL` but still a behavioral regression for permission grants.

File: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go, Line: 121, Issue: Redundant DB fetch: In `Check`, when `getCachedIdentityPermissions` succeeds but `checkPermission` returns false, the code falls through to `getIdentityPermissions`, which re-fetches permissions from the database (or via singleflight) and re-runs the check, before finally setting `permDenialCache`. This means every denied check with a warm `permCache` triggers a full DB round-trip on the first occurrence. This may be intentional (to confirm the denial against fresh data), but if so it partially defeats the purpose of the permission cache and adds latency to the denial path; consider setting the denial cache directly from the cached-permission result or documenting the double-check.

File: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go, Line: 948, Issue: Weak test assertion: The "Fallback to the database on outdated cache" test only asserts that access to dash2 is allowed. It does not verify that the cache is updated (or invalidated) after the database fallback, so a regression where the stale cache entry is left in place and repeatedly forces a DB lookup on every Check would not be caught. Consider asserting the post-check state of `permCache` (e.g., that dash2 is now cached) to make the test meaningful for the caching behavior it claims to cover.

findings: File: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go, Line: 98, Issue: Race condition: `CreateOrUpdateDevice` uses a check-then-act pattern: it counts devices, and if under the limit proceeds to insert. Two concurrent requests for different new devices can both observe `count < deviceLimit` and both insert, exceeding the limit. Since the limit is the core feature of this PR, a unique/atomic enforcement mechanism (or at least a re-check after insert) is needed for the limit to be reliable under concurrency.

File: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go, Line: 98, Issue: Error semantics: `CreateOrUpdateDevice` now returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` when the UPDATE affects 0 rows, but 0 rows affected can also mean the device row simply doesn't exist (or was deleted between the count and the update). Callers of `CreateOrUpdateDevice` cannot distinguish "limit reached" from "device missing", and a transient race (device deleted after the count) surfaces as a limit error. Consider returning a distinct error or falling back to insert when the row is absent.

File: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go, Line: 44, Issue: Latency on request path: TagDevice was previously run in a background goroutine with its own timeout, so it never blocked authentication. It is now called synchronously with the request context, meaning every anonymous request pays the full latency of the device-store write (and fails tagging entirely if the store is slow or the request context is cancelled mid-request). If this is intentional to enforce the device limit before returning an identity, consider whether a timeout or async-then-check design is still needed for the non-limit error path.

File: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go, Line: 44, Issue: Lost panic recovery: The removed goroutine had a recover() guard protecting authentication from a panic inside TagDevice. The new synchronous call has no such protection, so a panic in the device service now propagates into the authentication flow and can fail requests (e.g., a 500 on every anonymous request) instead of being logged and swallowed.

File: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go, Line: 147, Issue: Behavior change: `TagDevice` now returns the error from `tagDeviceUI` instead of only logging it at debug level and continuing. This changes the contract for all callers: previously a UI-tagging failure was non-fatal (the function always returned nil), and now it propagates. If any caller treats a non-nil return as a request failure (e.g., aborting a login flow), a transient UI-tagging error would now fail the whole request. Verify this propagation is intentional and that callers handle it, or keep the previous log-and-continue behavior.

Since backup codes are meant to be single-use, this should be done atomically (e.g., conditional update checking the previous value, or a transaction with row locking).

findings: File: packages/app-store/index.ts, Line: 3, Issue: Type change: modules to Promises: Each entry in `appStore` changed from a module namespace object (synchronous `import * as x`) to a `Promise<module>` (dynamic `import()`). Any consumer that accesses `appStore.googlecalendar` (or any other entry) synchronously now receives a Promise instead of the module, so property access like `appStore.googlecalendar.add` will be `undefined` and calls will fail at runtime. All call sites must now `await` each entry (e.g., `(await appStore.googlecalendar).add`). If the consuming code elsewhere in this PR was updated accordingly this is fine, but any call site not shown here that still uses the old synchronous shape will break. Also note the commented-out `example` entry changed name from `_example` to `example` — harmless since it's commented, but worth confirming the directory actually exists if it's ever re-enabled.

File: packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts, Line: 125, Issue: Unawaited async callback: The `forEach` callback is now `async`, but `Array.prototype.forEach` does not await the returned promises. The calendar `deleteEvent` (and any other async work in the callback) will run fire-and-forget: `Reschedule` can complete before deletions finish, and any rejection from `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` becomes an unhandled promise rejection with no way for the caller to observe the failure. Use `for...of` with `await`, or `Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` if parallel deletion is intended.

File: packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts, Line: 125, Issue: Unawaited async callback: The `forEach` callback is now `async`, but `Array.prototype.forEach` does not await promises returned from its callback. The `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` and `deleteMeeting(...)` promises are therefore fire-and-forget: the outer `try` block cannot catch their rejections, so a failed calendar/video deletion is silently swallowed (unhandled promise rejection) and `Reschedule` may report success before deletions complete. If sequential/awaited deletion is intended, use a `for...of` loop (or `Promise.all` with `map`) so errors are handled by the surrounding `try/catch`.

File: packages/core/CalendarManager.ts, Line: 28, Issue: Unawaited promise: `getCalendar` is now asynchronous (it returns a Promise), but in `getCalendarCredentials` the result is still assigned synchronously: `const calendar = getCalendar(credential)`. The object stored in the returned array therefore holds a Promise in its `calendar` field. The one visible consumer (`getConnectedCalendars`) was updated to `await item.calendar`, but any other caller of `getCalendarCredentials` that reads `calendar` synchronously will now receive a Promise instead of the calendar instance (or null), silently changing behavior. Consider awaiting `getCalendar` here (e.g., via `Promise.all` over the map) so the returned shape stays non-Promise.

File: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts, Line: 458, Issue: await inside forEach: The refactor to async `getCalendar` places an `await` inside a `forEach(async (credential) => ...)`
callback. `forEach` does not wait for the returned promises, so the enclosing handler continues
(and can complete) before the calendar deletions for recurring bookings finish; any rejection from
`getCalendar` or `deleteEvent` becomes an unhandled rejection. Since the PR already converted the
sibling old-behaviour block to a `for...of` loop for exactly this reason, this block should use the
same pattern (or `Promise.all` with `map`).

File: packages/lib/payment/deletePayment.ts, Line: 16, Issue: Suspicious await: The change adds `await` to a plain index lookup into `appStore`. If `appStore` values are synchronous module objects (as the surrounding type usage `"lib" in paymentApp` suggests), the `await` is a no-op and does not actually perform an async import — the module is still loaded eagerly wherever `appStore` is defined, so the stated goal of "async import" is not achieved by this line. Conversely, if `appStore` values were changed to promises elsewhere in the PR, the declared type (`keyof typeof appStore` resolving to a module shape) would now be inaccurate and TypeScript would not catch misuse of `paymentApp`. Either way, this line alone does not implement async loading; verify how `appStore` is populated.

File: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx, Line: 553, Issue: Possible Bug: `forEach` does not await the callback, so making it `async` does not make the loop asynchronous. The `await getCalendar(...)` inside only suspends within the callback; the surrounding code continues immediately, and the returned promises from `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` are never awaited or collected. Consequences: (1) the caller may respond/complete before calendar events are actually deleted, and (2) any rejection inside the async callbacks becomes an unhandled promise rejection that is invisible to the caller's error handling. Use `for...of` with `await`, or `Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` if parallel deletion is intended.

File: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx, Line: 553, Issue: Unhandled async errors: With the `forEach(async ...)` change, errors thrown by `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent` (e.g., network failure deleting a calendar event during reschedule) no longer propagate to the tRPC procedure's error handling; they surface as unhandled promise rejections. The user would see the reschedule succeed while deletions silently failed. This is the same root cause as the non-awaited `forEach` and is fixed by awaiting the loop.

findings: 1\. Kafka test uses confluent_kafka 📘 Rule violation ✓ Correctness New Kafka-related tests use real confluent_kafka Producer/Consumer and topic admin operations instead of Arroyo LocalProducer with MemoryMessageStorage. This violates the required Kafka/Arroyo testing approach and can make tests slower and more brittle.

2\. Shutdown skips queued items 🐞 Bug ⛯ Reliability FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets worker.shutdown=True, so OrderedQueueWorker.run can exit its loop without draining remaining queued items; those offsets remain outstanding and won’t be processed/committed. This can drop in-flight work during graceful shutdown and cause reprocessing on restart.

3\. Join drops in-flight work 🐞 Bug ⛯ Reliability SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.join calls close(), which stops the commit thread and immediately shuts down the queue pool without waiting for queued items to finish or flushing a final commit. This makes graceful shutdown lose uncommitted progress and can reprocess messages after restart.

4\. Unbounded queue memory growth 🐞 Bug ⛯ Reliability FixedQueuePool creates unbounded queue.Queue instances and submit() always put()s, so high input rates can accumulate unlimited in-memory backlog instead of applying backpressure. This contradicts the strategy’s stated “natural backpressure” and the repo’s established MessageRejected-based backpressure approach.

findings: 1\. Meet fallback crashes 🐞 Bug ✓ Correctness EventManager.create reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without checking if the destinationCalendar array is empty, causing a runtime exception when destinationCalendar is []/null. This can crash booking flows (including reminders/webhooks) that now frequently set destinationCalendar to an empty array.

2\. Externalcalendarid not recorded 🐞 Bug ✓ Correctness EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents does not pass destination.externalId into CalendarManager.createEvent when destination.credentialId is missing, so EventResult.externalId remains undefined and booking references are created without externalCalendarId. Subsequent update/delete operations that rely on reference.externalCalendarId can fail or target the wrong calendar.

3\. Collective calendars dropped 🐞 Bug ✓ Correctness handleNewBooking initializes evt.destinationCalendar to null when the organizer and eventType have no destinationCalendar, and then attempts to push teamDestinationCalendars via optional chaining, which becomes a no-op. This prevents creating calendar events for collective hosts when only the hosts (not the organizer) have connected calendars.

4\. Google createevent patch mismatch 🐞 Bug ⛯ Reliability GoogleCalendarService.createEvent inserts into selectedCalendar || "primary" but later patches using calendarId: selectedCalendar, which can be undefined when no destinationCalendar matches the provided credentialId. This makes the follow-up patch call target an undefined calendarId even though the event was created on primary.

5\. Google calendarid resolves undefined 🐞 Bug ✓ Correctness GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent/deleteEvent compute the calendarId by comparing `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` even when externalCalendarId is null/undefined, which can only produce undefined and breaks the Google API calls. This impacts reschedule/cancel flows when reference.externalCalendarId is missing or not provided.

6\. Organization slug not persisted 🐞 Bug ✓ Correctness Organization creation only writes Team.slug when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, leaving slug null when the flag is false despite validating slug uniqueness and using slug for downstream org lookups. This makes newly created orgs unreachable by slug in slug-based APIs.

7\. Recurring cancel misses calendars 🐞 Bug ⛯ Reliability In the recurring-cancel path, cancellation deletes only the first calendar reference per updated booking by using .find() on updBooking.references, leaving additional host calendar events undeleted. Because the recurring deletion is nested inside a loop over all calendar references, it can also repeat the same deletion work multiple times for multi-host bookings.

findings: Using `assert` for runtime validation is unsafe because assertions are disabled when Python runs with the `-O` (optimize) flag. If `message.value` is not a `BrokerValue`, this will silently pass and cause an `AttributeError` on the next line instead of a clear error.

`queue.ShutDown` was introduced in Python 3.13. If Sentry targets Python 3.11 or 3.12, this will raise `AttributeError` at runtime. The same applies to `q.shutdown(immediate=False)` on line 238. Verify that the minimum supported Python version is 3.13, or add a compatibility shim (e.g., catch `AttributeError` or check `hasattr(queue, 'ShutDown')`).

`join` calls `close()`, which shuts down the commit thread and the queue pool. The arroyo framework typically calls `close()` first and then `join()` to wait for completion. Calling `close()` from `join()` means the queue pool is shut down a second time and `commit_thread.join()` is called again. More importantly, `join` semantically should only wait for in-flight work to complete, not initiate shutdown. Consider implementing `join` to wait for the queue pool to drain rather than delegating to `close()`.

The test docstring states "errors in processing don't block offset commits for other messages," but the assertion checks that no commits happened for `test_partition`. These are contradictory. Because `OrderedQueueWorker.run` has a `finally` block that always calls `complete_offset` (even on exception), both offsets 100 and 101 will be marked complete, and the commit loop will commit offset 101. The assertion should instead verify that commits DO happen (i.e., the error doesn't block the subsequent successful message from being committed).

The denial cache key uses `_` as a delimiter between all components without any escaping. If `name` or `parent` contain `_`, keys can collide. For example, `name="dash_1"` with `parent="fold"` produces the same suffix as `name="dash"` with `parent="1_fold"`. While Grafana UIDs typically use hyphens, this is worth hardening — consider using a delimiter that cannot appear in UIDs (e.g., `/` or `\x00`), or use `fmt.Sprintf` with a structured format.

findings: `complete_offset` is called unconditionally in the `finally` block, even when `result_processor` raises. That makes failed work items appear successfully processed and allows the commit loop to advance offsets, potentially skipping/losing messages. Only mark the offset completed after the work item was processed successfully (and avoid completing on shutdown paths).

`get_committable_offsets` can incorrectly commit past missing offsets after a prior commit. After `mark_committed` prunes offsets ≤ committed, `min_offset` may jump forward over a gap, and `start = max(last_committed + 1, min_offset)` will skip the missing offset and allow committing later ones (e.g. seen {100,102,103} -> commit 100 -> next min_offset=102 -> commit through 103). Add an explicit gap check so we never advance commits past `last_committed + 1` unless that offset has been observed and completed.

The thread-queue-parallel strategy starts a background commit thread; this test only calls `factory.shutdown()` (which stops the queue workers) but never closes the returned `consumer`, so the commit thread can keep running and mutate state after assertions (and leak into other tests). Close the strategy before shutting down the factory (and apply similarly in the other new thread-queue-parallel tests).

It wires the new mode into the existing consumer factory/CLI configuration and adds unit/integration tests to validate ordering and offset commit behavior. **Changes:** - Add a `FixedQueuePool` + `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` implementation to process grouped work items in parallel while maintaining per-group ordering.

findings: `device_limit` is read from `[auth.anonymous]`, but it is not present in `conf/defaults.ini`’s `[auth.anonymous]` section (see `conf/defaults.ini:581-593`). Without that, the new setting is undiscoverable for users and won’t appear in the default config shipped with Grafana.

Device-limit enforcement is currently non-atomic: `CountDevices(...)` is executed and then an `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT` is performed. Under concurrency, multiple requests can observe `count < limit` and insert/update concurrently, temporarily exceeding the configured limit. This also adds an extra COUNT query to every tagged request when the limit is enabled.

The new test only asserts that inserting a *new* device fails once the limit is reached. It doesn’t verify the intended behavior that an *existing* device can still be updated when the limit is reached (the `updateDevice` path). findings: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` can be `undefined` when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`/`[]`. Accessing `.integration` will throw and break booking creation/reschedule for Meet location. Use optional chaining (or a guard) so the fallback works even when no destination calendar is selected.

`credentialId` is now only set on references when `isCalendarType` is true. Video references rely on `credentialId` for later cleanup (e.g. cancellation uses `bookingVideoReference.credentialId`), so dropping it will prevent deleting/updating the created video meeting.

If a calendar reference has `credentialId` but that credential isn't present in `this.calendarCredentials` and also can't be fetched from DB, `credential` stays undefined and `updateEvent(credential, ...)` will throw a non-obvious runtime error. Add an explicit guard (or return a failure result) before calling `updateEvent`.

`selectedCalendar` can be `undefined` when `destinationCalendar` doesn't contain an entry for the passed `credentialId`. In that case the insert uses the fallback to "primary", but the later `events.patch({ calendarId: selectedCalendar })` will be called with `undefined` and can fail. Default `selectedCalendar` to "primary" when not found.

In `updateEvent`, `externalCalendarId` can be `null`/empty (it’s passed from booking references). The current fallback branch searches for `externalId === externalCalendarId` (which will be `null/undefined`) and can produce an `undefined` calendarId, causing the Google API call to fail. Provide a reliable fallback (e.g. destination calendar’s first externalId, then "primary").

In `deleteEvent`, the fallback path tries to find a destinationCalendar entry matching `externalCalendarId` even when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, resulting in `undefined` and relying on later ternaries. Simplify and make the fallback explicit to avoid deleting from the wrong calendar.

`evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither event type nor organizer has a destination calendar, but later collective logic appends team members via `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)`. If organizer has no destination calendar, team host destination calendars will be dropped. Prefer an empty array so the collective append always works.

When `dynamicUserList` is missing/empty for a dynamic booking, this currently throws a generic `Error` and gets converted into a 500 "Unable to load users". That’s a client input problem and should return a 400 with a clear message.

This inverts the org slug behavior compared to the existing publish/update flow. Setting `slug` directly here under team billing likely bypasses that flow.

In the recurring-event branch, the code already iterates all calendar credentials and deletes events for all `updatedBookings`. When there are multiple `_calendar` references, the surrounding loop will repeat that same work for each reference, causing duplicate delete calls and unnecessary API load. Exit the loop after completing the recurring deletion pass.

With `destinationCalendar` now an array and `Calendar.createEvent` receiving `credentialId`, this implementation always uses the *first* destination calendar. When `EventManager` iterates multiple destinations, Office365 event creation for non-primary hosts can end up using the wrong `externalId` (or a different integration’s externalId) and create on the wrong calendar / 404. Select the destination calendar that matches the passed `credentialId` (fallback to the first).

Same issue as other calendar services: this always uses the first element of `event.destinationCalendar`. For collective/multi-host bookings, `EventManager` will call `createEvent` once per destination/credential; without selecting by `credentialId`, Lark event creation for secondary hosts can target the wrong calendar ID. Update the signature to accept `credentialId` and pick the matching destination calendar (fallback to first).

findings: Using `forEach(async ...)` here means the delete operations are not awaited; the handler can proceed to send emails / return before calendar/video deletions finish, and any rejection becomes unhandled. Use `await Promise.all(...)` (or a `for...of` loop) so side effects complete and errors propagate predictably.

`forEach(async ...)` inside the `try` block is not awaited, so calendar/video deletions can continue after the function proceeds, and exceptions inside the async callback will not be caught by this `try/catch`. Await the work (e.g., `await Promise.all(...)`) so failures are handled and deletions complete before continuing.

`forEach(async ...)` is not awaited, so deletions may still be running after the function continues, and errors thrown in the async callback will not be caught by the surrounding `try/catch`. Switch to an awaited pattern (`await Promise.all(...)` or `for...of`).

This branch uses `forEach(async ...)` and awaits deletions inside the callback, but the outer flow never awaits those promises. That can lead to missed/late deletions (and unhandled rejections) because `apiDeletes` may be awaited before it is fully populated. Use a `for...of` loop (or an awaited `Promise.all`) and push the deletion promises directly.

`getVideoAdapters` now awaits each app module sequentially in a loop. When `withCredentials` contains multiple credentials (e.g., for availability aggregation), this serializes imports and can increase latency. Consider importing/building adapters in parallel with `Promise.all` and filtering nulls.
